title: Sleepless Night
subtitle: No one wields greater power than she, for she is the mother.

items.text: The motel hallway is as quiet as ever. The maid stands, smiling.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Did you see it?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: My baby, of course. Oh, so it didn't show up, then? What a shy little pumpkin!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What is it exactly?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: A supernatural being, an amalgam of urban legends, an ever-pounding heart, and a shy little baby—all under one roof.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But seeing how you got out of there in one piece, I'm certain you've already earned its approval. Come on in. I'll show you the sweetest little room in the motel.
A red door appears behind her.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Don't be afraid, sweetheart. Go ahead. Open the door.
The door remains motionless.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Open it. Now.
The mercenary says nothing. She silently wipes the barrel of her gun.
*bang-bang*
She fires two shots at the red door.
The entire motel trembles violently.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That'll do it.
Before she can reload, the ground starts to shake beneath her feet, and a deafening sound reverberates through the hallway.
The maid's eyes widen in surprise.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Why didn't I think of that?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Your eyes haven't recovered yet, have they? Tsk, Tsk. Such poor aim.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Let me lend you a hand.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Listen to Mama.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I told you long ago about the consequences of disobedience.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, it's out of bullets. Could you help me reload?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, my sweet child.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Can you see it? This is the beauty of fear.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Watch out!

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Please, come in, my dear guests.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: You'll find what you seek inside.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: When I found it, it was still called Sweet Home.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: It was all alone, abandoned in the wilderness. The poor little thing.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So you took it in? Some unknown, growing arcane consciousness that takes the form of a motel yet somehow also exists as a baby?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Yes.
The maid bends down and picks up the swaddled baby from the crib.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: There, there.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But it's seriously impacted the lives of the locals.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, Ms. Vertin, they chose to come here of their own volition. I never forced them to stay.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But after leaving, some of them went mad or even committed suicide.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Well, they made those decisions themselves.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Now is not the time to dwell on such trivial matters, Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Haven't you been searching for Ms. Barbara?
She points to the open door.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Don't get any bright ideas, maid.
Her eye shines emerald again as she presses the barrel of her shotgun against Tuesday's back.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: If Vertin gets so much as a scratch, I'll blast your chest open.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Along with your baby.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Go inside, boss. I'll keep an eye on her.
Red curtains cover every inch of the room, like flesh clinging to a body. An ivory bed stands in the center.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Here you are, Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I'm so glad. I was beginning to think I'd never regain contact with the outside world.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ms. Argus, you can put your gun down now.
She speaks, trembling slightly as she savors every moment of her heightened heartrate.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I've shown my utmost sincerity, have I not?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Shut your trap!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's get out of here, Ms. Barbara.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I don't think it's the wisest choice to have this conversation while we're still inside a living thing.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Argus, I need you to keep Tuesday in check until we make it out of here.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: You ain't gotta tell me twice.
A beam of light shines in through the window. Dawn is breaking.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I've gazed at this scenery countless times, but never have I felt as enthralled as today.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But, Ms. Vertin, don't you think you've forgotten something?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Forgotten what?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: That guest who came with you. Shortly after her arrival, she hurried off to that armament factory. She's such an impatient child. Luckily, she made her way back here.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Her name's Lilya, right?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What did you do to her?
The maid laughs softly.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Relax, she's fine. She's sleeping soundly as we speak, with or without nightmares.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Follow me. I'm sure she's eager to see you.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: This is the room.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Open it.
The maid finds the key on her keyring, puts it in the lock, and turns it.
Room 203, Tuesday's Motel
The room is empty.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh.
The maid frowns, her annoyance visible on her face.
The owner of the suitcase rushes to the window and looks down.
Lilya is sitting exhausted below. Their eyes meet.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Vertin! There you are!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Listen, those Manus scum have already wormed their way into the town. We can't go there.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You look terrible.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I couldn't sleep at all in that haunted room. Every time I closed my eyes, I saw all kinds of creepy stuff.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Can you come down here, Captain? Talking like this hurts my neck.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Okay.
